Legal Standards.legal_standard: Reservoir-Specific Storage and Cold Pool Management
Legal Standards.caption: Each reservoir operates under site-specific storage and operational specifications, which vary widely by facility and include management of the cold pool to maintain lower-temperature water for downstream uses and ecological protection.
Legal Standards.info: Each reservoir operates under site-specific storage and operational specifications, which vary widely by facility and include management of the cold pool to maintain lower-temperature water for downstream uses and ecological protection.

vocabulary.definition: Cold pool; definition: Deep reservoir water that maintains colder average temperatures due to sufficient depth; management objective: Temperature control for downstream releases

Legal Standards.legal_standard: State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB) Permitting Authority
Legal Standards.caption: SWRCB issues permits through separate regulatory processes for water diversion and water storage and monitors compliance with permit conditions governing reservoir releases.
Legal Standards.info: SWRCB issues permits through separate regulatory processes for water diversion and water storage and monitors compliance with permit conditions governing reservoir releases.

Legal Standards.caption: Reservoir releases may be managed discretionarily to satisfy multiple overlapping legal and operational objectives.
Legal Standards.info: Reservoir releases may be managed discretionarily to satisfy multiple overlapping legal and operational objectives.

vocabulary.definition: Salinity control, Compliance with senior water rights, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service requirements, Environmental Protection Agency requirements, Clean Water Act (CWA) compliance

Tier 1.threshold: Storage >= top threshold in >=90% of years (April values). As of July 2025, top threshold = 50th percentile of recent historical CDEC data.

policies.note: Triggers include water year type, biological monitoring, sediment transport, and water temperature; normal operations proceed under standard management.
Stored water is not curtailed; new diversions to storage can be curtailed based on constitutional priorities and rights in time.
Colder/deeper water is used strategically to maintain downstream temperature via mixing and multilevel pumping.

Tier 2.threshold: Storage >= middle threshold in >=67% of years (April values). As of July 2025, middle threshold = 33rd percentile of recent historical CDEC data.

policies.policy_name: Curtailments for junior water rights holders
policies.note: Curtailments occur primarily among junior water rights holders to ensure allocations for senior rights holders; carryover storage generally not in danger.

Triggers modifications to standard operating procedures, permit streamlining for water transfers and groundwater recharge, careful management of existing supplies, and water rights curtailments (even potentially for senior holders).

Tier 3.threshold: Storage >= middle threshold in >=30% of years (April values). As of July 2025, middle threshold = 33rd percentile of recent historical CDEC data.

policies.note: Major changes to operating procedures; state long-term drought/shortage plans implicated. Encouragement of local and regional planning for multi-year periods of little to no deliveries from state and federal projects.

Tier 4.threshold: Does not meet Tiers 1-3; storage below middle threshold (at or below lower threshold) in >70% of years (April values). As of July 2025, lower threshold = 20th percentile of recent historical values.

policies.policy_name: Extreme reservoir and water supply management
policies.note: Physical constraints like deadpool dominate operations; severe curtailments and operational modifications occur to preserve basic allocations, potentially affecting all rights holders.
